# Blog jordimariezcurrena.com Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build and deploy a multilingual (es/ca/en) Hugo blog with PaperMod, including an About page with a career timeline, a Contact page, a Projects section, full technical SEO, and automatic deploys to Cloudflare Pages.

**Architecture:** Static site generated by Hugo (extended) using the PaperMod theme installed as a Hugo Module. Content lives as Markdown with per-language file suffixes and translated slugs. Two small custom layouts (About with a data-driven timeline, Projects grid) extend PaperMod without touching its core files. Deploy is git-based: push to GitHub `main` → Cloudflare Pages builds and publishes; PRs get preview URLs.

**Tech Stack:** Hugo (extended) + Go (for Hugo Modules) + PaperMod theme + GitHub + Cloudflare Pages + Cloudflare Registrar/DNS.

**Reference spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-blog-jordimariezcurrena-design.md`

### Task 1: Install prerequisites

**Files:** none (tooling install only)

- [ ] **Step 1: Install Hugo extended and Go**

Run (PowerShell):
```powershell
winget install --id Hugo.Hugo.Extended -e
winget install --id GoLang.Go -e
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Verify installation**

Run:
```powershell
hugo version
go version
```
Expected: `hugo version` output contains `extended`; `go version` prints a Go version (1.21+).

- [ ] **Step 3: Record the exact Hugo version for later use**

Run:
```powershell
hugo version
```
Copy the version number shown (e.g. `v0.140.2`) — it will be used later as the `HUGO_VERSION` environment variable in Cloudflare Pages (Task 14), so the build environment matches what you tested locally.

No commit for this task (no repo files changed).

### Task 3: Add PaperMod via Hugo Modules

**Files:**
- Create: `go.mod`
- Modify: `hugo.toml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Initialize the Hugo Module**

Run:
```powershell
hugo mod init github.com/jordimariezcurrena/jordimariezcurrena.com
```
Expected: creates `go.mod` with a `module` line matching the repo path.

- [ ] **Step 2: Reference PaperMod in hugo.toml**

Add to `hugo.toml` (replacing the `theme = ...` line Hugo generated, since Hugo Modules replace the classic theme mechanism):

```toml
[module]
  [[module.imports]]
    path = "github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod"
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Fetch the module and build**

Run:
```powershell
hugo mod get -u
hugo
```
Expected: `hugo mod get -u` completes without error and updates `go.mod`/`go.sum`; `hugo` build succeeds and `public/index.html` references PaperMod's CSS (e.g. contains `stylesheet.css` or `core.css`).

Verify:
```powershell
Select-String -Path public/index.html -Pattern "papermod" -SimpleMatch
```
Expected: at least one match (PaperMod's asset paths include `papermod` in the filename hash or the theme's asset comment).

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```powershell
git add go.mod go.sum hugo.toml
git commit -m "Add PaperMod theme via Hugo Modules"
```

> **Post-implementation note (superseding the steps above):** Hugo's actual
> behavior on this project required 3 changes beyond what's written above,
> found and verified while implementing this task (commits `0a90e8e`,
> `ef68d1b`):
> 1. `url:` is a reserved Hugo front-matter field (page/permalink override)
>    and rejects external absolute URLs. The sample project's front matter
>    uses `link:` instead of `url:`, and `layouts/projects/list.html` reads
>    `.Params.link` instead of `.Params.url`.
> 2. A section's `slug:` front matter does not change the section's own
>    list-page URL — only `url:` does. `content/projects/_index.es.md` and
>    `_index.ca.md` each have `url: "/proyectos/"` / `url: "/ca/projectes/"`
>    added (in addition to `slug:`).
> 3. Leaf pages under a section don't inherit that `url:` override, so
>    `hugo.toml` gained per-language permalinks config so future projects
>    resolve at translated URLs automatically from `slug:` alone, with no
>    per-page override needed:
>    ```toml
>    [languages.es.permalinks]
>      projects = "/proyectos/:slug/"
>    [languages.ca.permalinks]
>      projects = "/projectes/:slug/"
>    [languages.en.permalinks]
>      projects = "/projects/:slug/"
>    ```
>
> **Known limitation, accepted and documented in code** (see the comment in
> `layouts/partials/templates/schema_json.html` above the `BreadcrumbList`
> logic): the JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` on ES/CA project leaf pages is missing
> its section-level parent entry, because that shared partial resolves
> ancestors by content-tree path, not rendered permalink. Fixing it properly
> means changing a partial shared by every page on the site — out of scope
> here. Visible breadcrumb navigation and hreflang are unaffected; this only
> affects one structured-data block.
>
> **Adding a future project:** only needs `title`, `slug`, `description`,
> `translationKey`, and `link` (if external) — no `hugo.toml` change and no
> `url:` override required, since the permalinks config above already
> handles translated leaf URLs for the whole section.
